The corona product keeps the triangle and gives each corner its own copy of H, the teal leaves Ax, Bx, and Cx for (A, x), (B, x), and (C, x), each joined to its corner by an accent edge. The result is the sunlet graph with 6 nodes and 6 edges." width="100%"} The corona product $G \circ H$ (Frucht and Harary, 1970) keeps this graph and attaches, to each of its nodes, a private copy of `other` whose nodes are all joined to that node. With a single-node `other` it adds a pendant leaf to every node; with a larger `other` every node gets its own little "crown". Coronas are used to build graphs with prescribed properties (domination, spectra, distance indices) and as models of networks where every hub serves its own local cluster. Both graphs must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [other]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph copied around each node. Neither graph is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph with `n + n * m` nodes. This graph's nodes keep their labels and attributes and get IDs `1` to `n` (in ID order); the copy of `other`'s j-th node at this graph's i-th node gets ID `n + i * m + j + 1`, label `"(g, h)"`, and `other`'s node attributes. Edges inside this graph and inside the copies keep their weight and attributes. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If either graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The product has $|E_G| + n(|E_H| + m)$ edges. Every node of this graph dominates its crown, so this graph's nodes form a dominating set of the corona. Matches NetworkX's `corona_product` (which, unlike EdgeCase, does not copy node attributes). ## Examples {.doc-examples} The corona of a triangle with a single node adds a pendant leaf at each corner (the "sunlet" graph): ::: {#c01f32dc .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec triangle = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) triangle.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A")]) leaf = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["x"]) sunlet = triangle.corona_product(leaf) sunlet.count_nodes(), sunlet.count_edges(), sunlet.get_edges_str_repr(use_labels=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (6, 6, ['A--B', 'B--C', 'C--A', 'A--(A, x)', 'B--(B, x)', 'C--(C, x)']) ``` ::: :::
